17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans ~ 1805 North Campbell Avenue, Chicago, IL
Proposed Zoning:  B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District

Lot Area: 8,975.52 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to redevelop the subject property with a new
four-story residential building containing twenty-one (21) dwelling units
and an attached garage. The proposed building will measure 44 ft.-1 in. in
height. The subject property is a Transit Served Location and will be
supported by eleven (11) off-street garage parking spaces and twenty-two
(22) bicycle parking spaces. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-0303-D optional
Administrative Adjustment and Variation and pursuant to Secs. 17-13-
1003-EE and 17-13-1101-B of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the
Applicant is seeking to reduce the off-street parking ratio for a Transit
Served Location to 50% (eleven (11) parking spaces for twenty-one (21)
residential units), reduce the rear setback for floors containing residential
units from 30 feet to 27 feet, reduce the east side setback to 4 ft., and is
seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the code, for the attached plans.

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 832 linear feet of the Western CTA Blue Line
Rail Station. The proposed residential building containing twenty-one (21) residential
units will be supported by eleven (11) off-street parking spaces and twenty-two (22) bicycle
parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to permit an
reduction in the number of required off-street parking spaces, from twenty-one (21) parking
spaces to eleven (11) parking spaces.

2. The proposed building design complies with the main building door and entryway design
standards provided by Sec. 17-4-0504. The proposed building will have a front setback of
7.5 feet from the subject lot’s front property line along West Bloomingdale Avenue to align
with the footprints of the neighboring buildings on the block. The building’s first floor was
designed with windows facing the sidewalk located along West Bloomingdale Avenue and
North Campbell Avenue.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
residential building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
proximity to the Western CTA Blue Line Rail Station. The Applicant believes the
redevelopment of an underutilized corner lot will improve conditions in the subject area
for residents and other commuters traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed residential building will contain a total of twenty-one (21) residential units.
Four (4) of the proposed units will be affordable units. The proposed building will be
supported by eleven (11) off-street parking spaces and twenty-two (22) bicycle parking
spaces. The Applicant is seeking administrative approval to permit the off-street parking
reduction pursuant to the eTOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed residential building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace an underutilized
corner lot with a new multi-unit residential building, which will provide new residential
housing to meet multi-unit market demand. Based on the subject property’s proximity to
a designated CTA Rail Station (Western Blue Line), the Applicant believes the project
provides transit options and otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and
Management Plan rules promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an
area in need.
